caption: A gust blows across a row of candles on a windowsill, and the flames bend sideways and two of them go out, leaving smoke trails.

sa.check: A row of candles stands on a windowsill.
Two of the flames go out.
Smoke trails rise from the ones that went out.
All the flames lean the same way.

pc.expect: All the flames lean the same way at the same moment as the gust reaches them, and the survivors straighten when it passes.
pc.fail: The flames lean in different directions at the same moment; or a flame leans against the way the others lean; or the flames stay leaning after the curtains and everything else have settled; or a flame leans while nothing else in the scene moves at all.

pc.expect: The flames that go out are the ones the gust flattened, and they go out during the gust.
pc.fail: A flame goes out before the gust reaches it; or a flame goes out while it stands straight and untouched; or the flames go out one after another over the clip with no gust; or a flame that went out relights during the same gust.

pc.expect: The smoke trails rise from the wicks that went out and the surviving flames point upward between gusts.
pc.fail: A smoke trail sinks down the candle and pools on the sill; or a trail pours downward off the sill; or a surviving flame points downward; or a trail hangs as a fixed shape without rising.

pc.expect: Once out a candle stays out and its smoke trail only rises and thins.
pc.fail: A candle relights by itself; or a trail runs back into its wick; or a flame flickers between lit and out after the gust has passed; or a wick's glow brightens into a flame with nothing touching it.

pc.expect: The candles keep their number and places and each keeps one wick; no flame detaches.
pc.fail: A flame separates from its wick and floats; or a second flame appears on one wick; or a candle vanishes; or a new candle appears on the sill.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The candles' colour, the sill and the window stay the same.
pc.fail: A candle changes colour; or the sill's surface changes; or the view through the window jumps to a different place.
